description: Codex computer use, decoupled from the app, for usage inside any harness.
summary: LCU pulls Codex's computer-use runtime out from under the ChatGPT desktop app and exposes it as a plain tool to whatever harness you're already running — Claude Code, Codex CLI, Pi — so you get window reads, clicks, screenshots, and optional Chrome control without being locked to one client. The approval design is what sells it: per-app grants that only a human at the keyboard can answer (Touch ID on macOS), the model literally cannot see or fake the approval pane, and the app hosting the agent is never auto-approved, which is the kind of trust boundary you need before wiring computer-use into something like PenguPool where you're fanning out sessions across a machine. It's small, local, and composable in exactly the way I want agent tooling to be.
